messages.author: affa918ed63b6275
messages.subject: Re: Plotting a barplot and legend separately
parts:
You can use the power of gtable like this:

```
p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(cyl, fill = factor(gear))) + geom_bar() +
facet_wrap(~am+vs, nrow = 1)
gt <- ggplot_gtable(ggplot_build(p))

pushViewport(viewport(layout = grid.layout(nrow = 4, ncol = 4)))

pushViewport(viewport(layout.pos.row = 3))
grid.draw(gt[, -15])
popViewport()

pushViewport(viewport(layout.pos.row = 4, layout.pos.col = 4))
grid.draw(gt[, 15])
popViewport()
```

kohske

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: Plotting a barplot and legend separately
parts:
Building off of Kohske's example, you can pull out the pieces of the original gtable, and put them into another gtable, so you don't have to mess with grid viewports.


library(gtable)
library(ggplot2)

p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(cyl, fill = factor(gear))) + geom_bar() + 
    facet_wrap(~am+vs, nrow = 1)
gt <- ggplot_gtable(ggplot_build(p))

# We can render gt
grid.newpage()
grid.draw(g)

# Display the layout of gt
gtable_show_layout(gt)



# Create the gtable with one col and two rows
g <- gtable(widths = unit(1, "null"), heights = unit(c(1, 1), "null"))

# Pull out all columns from gt, except the last column, which has the legend
# Put it on the first row of the new gtable
g <- gtable_add_grob(g, gt[, -15], t=1, l=1, b=1, r=1)

# Pull out the legend from gt, and put it in the second row of the new gtable
g <- gtable_add_grob(g, gt[4, 15], t=2, l=1, b=2, r=1)

# Draw the new gtable
grid.newpage()
grid.draw(g)

--Winston

parts: Thanks Winston for the following up.

Just another topic, can we have gtable creation by setting nrow and ncol, like:

g <- gtable(nrow = 1, nrow = 2)
g <- gtable(nrow = 1, nrow = 2, default.units = "mm")

they are equivalent to:

g <- gtable(widths = unit(1, "mm"), heights = unit(c(1, 1), "mm"))

kohske
